correctness.rationale: The quantitative tangent-angle supporting-line deficit is proved with an explicit uniform second-derivative bound on a central increment window. The source Holder/degree estimate converts it to a fractional-Willmore deficit, an exact Fourier calculation supplies the pi-2/3 spectral constant, and normalized outer parallel bodies convert tangent-angle deviation into curvature-radius H^{-1} deviation with the factor r/(1+r)^3. Integrating the source first-variation identity and substituting q=1-s gives the displayed constants. Signs, homogeneities, Fourier normalization, and equality case were checked separately.

originality.rationale: The 2026 fixed-perimeter sources establish the sharp maximization but no matching quantitative curvature-radius deficit was located. The closest recent stability result, arXiv:2605.07543, is local for nearly spherical sets and compares two fractional perimeters with t<1. Searches for fixed-perimeter fractional-perimeter stability, curvature-radius H^{-1} control, chord-functional deficits, fractional-Willmore deficits, and outer-parallel formulations found no equivalent global convex endpoint theorem. Extremely recent concurrent work and non-obvious endpoint implications remain explicit residual risks.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a newly solved sharp fixed-perimeter inequality to an explicit global quantitative stability statement in a natural smooth convex class, identifies an intrinsic negative-Sobolev curvature metric, and simultaneously supplies a quantitative deficit for the underlying chord functional.
